spans.s:
Nṛ-medha,^1 Nṛ-medhas,^2 is the name of a protégé of Agni
in the Rigveda,^3 where he also appears with Sumedhas in a
hymn that Griffith^4 with justice declares to be unintelligible.
In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā^1 he is an unsuccessful rival of
Parucchepa, and in the Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa^2 he is an
Āṅgirasa and a seer of Sāmans (Chants).
1) Rv. x. 80, 3; 132, 7; Taittirīya
Saṃhitā, ii. 5, 8, 3.
2) Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa, viii. 8, 21
et seq.
3) x. 80, 3.
4) x. 132; Griffith, Hymns of the
Rigveda, 2, 578, n.

160; Hopkins, Transactions of the Connecti-
cut Academy of Arts and Sciences, 15, 61.
